items.q: What is a square foot?
items.a: A **square foot (sq ft)** is the area of a square 1 foot by 1 foot (about 30.5 cm × 30.5 cm). Dubai developers and portals usually quote unit sizes and prices **per sq ft**, even though DLD records areas in square metres.
items.kw: sqft sq ft square feet definition

items.q: What is a square metre?
items.a: A **square metre (sqm, m²)** is a square 1 m × 1 m. **1 sqm = 10.764 sq ft.** DLD transaction data, title deeds and many official documents use sqm, so convert before comparing with a brochure in sq ft.
items.kw: sqm m2 square meter metre definition

items.q: How do I convert square metres to square feet?
items.a: Multiply by **10.764**. Example: 100 sqm × 10.764 = **1,076 sq ft**. Quick mental check: sqm × 10, then add about 7.6%.
items.kw: convert sqm to sqft conversion formula

items.q: How do I convert square feet to square metres?
items.a: Divide by **10.764** (or multiply by 0.0929). Example: 1,000 sq ft ÷ 10.764 = **92.9 sqm**.
items.kw: convert sqft to sqm conversion formula

items.q: How do I convert price per sq ft to price per sqm (and back)?
items.a:
- **Price per sqm = price per sq ft × 10.764**
- **Price per sq ft = price per sqm ÷ 10.764**

Example: AED 1,800/sq ft × 10.764 = AED 19,375/sqm. Always convert before comparing DLD data (often per sqm) with a brochure (per sq ft).
items.kw: psf psm price per square meter conversion

items.q: What is built-up area (BUA)?
items.a: **Built-up area** is the area of the unit including its internal walls and usually its balcony/terrace. In Dubai brochures it often appears as **'Total area'** = internal (suite) area + balcony. Definitions vary by developer, so always check what's included on the floor plan and the SPA.
items.kw: bua built up area total area definition

items.q: What is suite area / internal area?
items.a: **Suite (internal) area** is the enclosed living space of the apartment, without the balcony or terrace. Floor plans typically show **Suite + Balcony = Total**. Use suite area to compare liveable space between projects.
items.kw: suite area internal area net area

items.q: What is carpet area, and is it used in Dubai?
items.a: **Carpet area** is the floor you can actually cover with carpet: wall-to-wall usable space, excluding walls, columns, shafts and the balcony. It's an Indian/Asian term; **Dubai brochures use suite/internal area and total area** instead. Usable carpet area is a bit smaller than suite area because walls and columns take space.
items.kw: carpet area usable area definition dubai

items.q: A unit's total built-up is 2,000 sq ft. How much is the carpet area apart from the balcony?
items.a:
Start from the floor plan:

1. **Internal (suite) area = total − balcony.** Example: 2,000 − 250 balcony = **1,750 sq ft** internal.
2. **Carpet (usable) area** is less than that, because walls, columns and service shafts take space. There's no legal fixed ratio in Dubai; it depends on the design.

Tell clients the suite area from the floor plan and avoid quoting a 'carpet' figure the developer hasn't published.
items.kw: carpet area 2000 sqft built up balcony how much usable

items.q: What is the difference between total area, suite area and balcony area?
items.a:
- **Suite/internal area:** enclosed living space
- **Balcony/terrace area:** outdoor space
- **Total area:** suite + balcony (what most prices per sq ft are calculated on)

Two units with the same total can have very different suite areas if one has a big terrace.
items.kw: total area suite area balcony difference

items.q: What is plot area?
items.a: **Plot area** is the land area of a villa/townhouse plot (or a building plot), usually in sq ft or sqm. It differs from the villa's **BUA**, which is the built floor area across all levels.

items.q: What is GFA (gross floor area)?
items.a: **GFA** is the total floor area a building or plot is allowed to have, across all floors, as set by the planning authority/master developer. It's used for land and development deals, not for selling individual units.

items.q: What is the difference between plot area and BUA for a villa?
items.a: **Plot area** = the land. **BUA** = the floor area built on it, summed over all floors. Example: a 3,000 sq ft plot may carry a villa with 3,800 sq ft BUA over two floors. Price per sq ft is normally quoted on BUA for villas; compare like with like.

items.q: How is price per sq ft calculated?
items.a: **Price per sq ft = price ÷ area in sq ft.** Example: AED 1,500,000 ÷ 1,000 sq ft = **AED 1,500/sq ft**. Check which area the developer uses (total incl. balcony or suite only) before comparing projects.
items.kw: price per sqft calculation psf formula

items.q: Why can a unit look cheap per sq ft but not be good value?
items.a:
Common reasons:

- A **big balcony/terrace** inflates total area
- **Poor layout** (long corridors, odd shapes) wastes space
- **Weaker location** inside the community
- **Higher service charges**

Compare suite area, layout efficiency and the area's DLD price per sq ft, not only the headline number.

items.q: What does 'efficiency' of a floor plan mean?
items.a: Efficiency is how much of the area is genuinely usable. A rough check: **suite area ÷ total area**, and how much of the suite is corridors. There's no official standard; compare floor plans of similar units side by side.

items.q: What do the abbreviations on Dubai floor plans mean (BR, M, L, D, K)?
items.a: Typical labels: **BR** bedroom, **M/MBR** master bedroom, **L/LR** living, **D** dining, **K** kitchen, **W** wardrobe/walk-in, **B/WC** bathroom, **P** powder room, **S/ST** store, **L/R** laundry, **MR** maid's room, **BAL** balcony. Labels vary; check the legend.
items.kw: floor plan abbreviations br mbr maid room

items.q: What is a studio apartment?
items.a: A unit with **one main room** combining living and sleeping, plus a separate bathroom and usually a kitchenette. In Dubai, studios are popular for rental investors because of their low entry price.

items.q: What is a '1+study' or '2+maid' unit?
items.a: An extra room that isn't a full bedroom: a **study** (often no window) or a **maid's room** (small room with its own bathroom). They add usable space but are not counted as bedrooms on the title.

items.q: What is a duplex?
items.a: An apartment on **two levels** connected by an internal staircase. Area is counted across both floors.

items.q: What is a penthouse?
items.a: A premium unit on the **top floor(s)** of a building, usually with larger terraces and higher ceilings. Price per sq ft is typically higher than lower floors.

items.q: What is a townhouse?
items.a: A house sharing **one or two walls** with neighbours, usually 2–3 floors with a small garden. Sold freehold with its plot in Dubai master communities.

items.q: What is the difference between a villa and a townhouse?
items.a: A **villa** is detached (no shared walls) on its own plot; a **townhouse** shares walls (end units share one wall). Villas usually have larger plots and command higher prices.

items.q: What does 'G+4' or 'B+G+20' mean?
items.a: Building height notation: **B** basement, **G** ground, **P** podium levels, then the number of upper floors. 'B+G+4P+20' = basement, ground, 4 podium (often parking) and 20 residential floors.

items.q: What is a podium in a building?
items.a: The lower floors of a tower, usually used for **parking, retail or amenities**, with the residential tower above. Units on podium level often have large terraces.

items.q: How many sq ft is a typical 1-bedroom in Dubai?
items.a: It varies by project and segment. Many new 1-bedroom apartments are roughly **600–900 sq ft** total, but luxury projects can be much larger. Always quote the actual size from the floor plan.

items.q: How many sq ft is a typical 2-bedroom in Dubai?
items.a: Roughly **1,000–1,400 sq ft** total for many mid-market projects; premium projects can be larger. Use the floor plan, not averages, with clients.

items.q: How do I measure area from a floor plan drawing?
items.a: Use the **areas printed on the plan** (suite, balcony, total). Don't scale-measure drawings: they're 'not to scale' indicative plans. The SPA states the contracted area.
items.kw: measure floor plan scale not to scale

items.q: What happens if the final area at handover is different from the SPA?
items.a: Most SPAs allow a **small variance** (often a few percent) with a price adjustment per sq ft beyond that. The exact tolerance is in the SPA, so read the clause before signing. DLD's title deed shows the final area.

items.q: Does the balcony area count in the price?
items.a: Usually yes: in most Dubai sales the price per sq ft is on **total area including balcony**. Check the SPA and price list. When comparing, also compute price per sq ft on suite area only.

items.q: What is ceiling height and why does it matter?
items.a: Floor-to-ceiling height affects how spacious a unit feels. Standard apartments are often around 2.7–3 m; premium units higher. Developers state it in the specifications if it's a selling point.

items.q: What is a hectare and an acre in sq ft?
items.a:
- **1 hectare = 10,000 sqm = 107,639 sq ft**
- **1 acre = 43,560 sq ft ≈ 4,047 sqm**

Useful for master-plan sizes and land deals.

items.q: What is the conversion between feet and metres?
items.a: **1 m = 3.281 ft; 1 ft = 0.3048 m.** For areas use the squared factor: 1 sqm = 10.764 sq ft.

items.q: How do I compare a project's price with the area average?
items.a:
1. Get the project's **price per sq ft** (price ÷ total area)
2. Get the **area's average** from DLD sales for the same unit type and period (DealPro: Market statistics / Price map)
3. **Difference % = (project − area) ÷ area × 100**

Explain any premium: brand, finishes, view, amenities, payment plan.
items.kw: compare psf area average premium discount

items.q: What is the difference between saleable area and title deed area?
items.a: **Saleable area** is what the developer sells on (often incl. balcony). The **title deed area** is what DLD registers after completion. They should match within the SPA tolerance.

items.q: What is a 'plot' sale in Dubai?
items.a: Buying **land** (a plot) to build on, usually with a permitted GFA and use. It's a different product from off-plan units, with its own fees and building obligations.

items.q: How do I explain 'price per sq ft' to a first-time buyer?
items.a: Simple version: **'It's the price of one square foot of the home.'** It lets you compare homes of different sizes fairly. A 1,000 sq ft unit at AED 1.5M and a 1,200 sq ft unit at AED 1.8M both cost AED 1,500 per sq ft.

items.q: What is a 'corner unit' and does it cost more?
items.a: A unit at the building's corner, often with **two facades** (more light/views). Developers often price corners slightly higher.

items.q: What is the 'view premium'?
items.a: Extra price for better views (sea, lagoon, golf, Burj Khalifa, park) or higher floors. Developers build it into floor-by-floor price lists; resale buyers also pay for views.

items.q: What is a floor rise?
items.a: A price increase per floor going up the building (e.g. a fixed amount or % per floor) set by the developer's price list.

items.q: What is DLD?
items.a: The **Dubai Land Department**: the government body that registers all property ownership and transactions in Dubai, collects the registration fees and runs services like Oqood, title deeds and the Dubai REST app. RERA is its regulatory arm.

items.q: What is the Dubai REST app?
items.a: DLD's official app for owners, buyers and brokers: check **project status (Mashrooi)**, broker licences, title deeds, service charges, rental index, and do some transactions online.

items.q: What is Mashrooi?
items.a: DLD's **project status service** (in Dubai REST / DLD website): shows a project's registration, escrow account, construction completion % and expected completion date.

items.q: What is an SPA?
items.a: The **Sale and Purchase Agreement**: the contract between buyer and developer (or seller) setting out price, payment plan, unit details, completion date, penalties and handover terms. It's registered with DLD for off-plan (Oqood).

items.q: What is an MOU in Dubai property?
items.a: A **Memorandum of Understanding**: for resales it's the RERA **Form F** signed by buyer and seller, setting price, deposit and transfer date.

items.q: What is a title deed?
items.a: The DLD document proving **ownership of a completed property**. For off-plan, ownership is first recorded on Oqood and converted to a title deed after completion.

items.q: What is an e-title deed?
items.a: The electronic version of the title deed issued by DLD, verifiable online. It has the same legal effect as the paper deed.

items.q: What is a NOC?
items.a: A **No Objection Certificate**. In property it usually means the **developer's NOC** confirming no dues and allowing a transfer/resale. Banks also issue NOCs/liability letters for mortgaged units.

items.q: What is an escrow account?
items.a: A **project-specific bank account** (approved by DLD) where buyers' payments for an off-plan project are held and released for that project's construction, under Law No. 8 of 2007.

items.q: What is Trakheesi?
items.a: DLD's **permit system for real estate advertising**. Each ad needs a Trakheesi permit number (usually shown with a QR code).

items.q: What is a BRN?
items.a: The **Broker Registration Number**: a RERA broker card number for an individual agent. It should appear on ads and documents.

items.q: What is an ORN?
items.a: The **Office Registration Number** of a licensed real estate brokerage in Dubai.

items.q: What is Ejari?
items.a: Dubai's official **tenancy contract registration** system. Registering a lease on Ejari is required for things like DEWA connection, visas and disputes.

items.q: What is Mollak?
items.a: DLD/RERA's system for **jointly owned property**: service charge budgets, owners' association accounts and payments.

items.q: What is an owners' association (OA)?
items.a: The body of **all owners in a jointly owned building/community**, managed by a RERA-registered management company, which runs common areas and collects service charges.

items.q: What is a master developer?
items.a: The developer of the **whole master community** (roads, infrastructure, master plan), e.g. Emaar for Dubai Hills Estate. Sub-developers may build individual projects inside it.

items.q: What is a sub-developer?
items.a: A developer building a project **inside another developer's master community**, under the master developer's rules and approvals.

items.q: What is a master community?
items.a: A large planned development (e.g. Dubai Hills Estate, Emaar South, Damac Hills) with its own master plan, infrastructure and community fees.

items.q: What is freehold?
items.a: Full ownership of the property (and, for villas, the land) **without time limit**, available to foreigners in Dubai's designated freehold areas.

items.q: What is leasehold?
items.a: A long lease (in Dubai often up to **99 years**) giving the right to use and benefit from a property, but not outright ownership.

items.q: What is usufruct?
items.a: A right to **use and benefit** from someone else's property for a fixed period (in Dubai up to 99 years), without owning it.

items.q: What is musataha?
items.a: A right to **build on and use land** owned by someone else, for a set period (up to 50 years, renewable, under Dubai law).

items.q: What is EOI?
items.a: **Expression of Interest**: a refundable-or-not deposit (per developer terms) to queue for a new launch before units are allocated.

items.q: What is a booking form / reservation form?
items.a: The developer's first document reserving a unit after the EOI or on direct sale, with the buyer's details and the booking amount. The SPA follows.

items.q: What is a payment plan?
items.a: The developer's **schedule of instalments** for an off-plan unit: down payment, construction-linked or dated instalments, handover payment and sometimes post-handover payments.

items.q: What is a post-handover plan (PHPP)?
items.a: A plan where part of the price is paid **after the keys are handed over**, typically over 1–5 years.

items.q: What is a construction-linked payment plan?
items.a: Instalments tied to **construction milestones** (e.g. 20% at foundation, 10% at structure 50%). DLD-inspected progress triggers payments.

items.q: What is handover?
items.a: The point when the completed unit is **delivered to the buyer**: final payment, inspection, keys, title deed and utility connections.

items.q: What is a completion certificate?
items.a: Issued by the relevant authority when a building is completed and fit for occupation. Handover and title deeds follow.

items.q: What is DLP (defects liability period)?
items.a: The period after completion when the developer must fix defects. Under Dubai law, **1 year for installations** and **10 years for structural defects**.

items.q: What is decennial liability?
items.a: The **10-year liability** of contractors/engineers (and developers to buyers) for structural defects or collapse.

items.q: What is service charge?
items.a: The annual fee owners pay (per sq ft) for **common area maintenance, security, cleaning, insurance and reserve funds**, approved by RERA.

items.q: What is a sinking/reserve fund?
items.a: Part of the service charge saved for **major future repairs and replacements** (lifts, roofs, façades).

items.q: What is a chiller fee / district cooling?
items.a: Many buildings are cooled by a **district cooling provider** (e.g. Empower). Residents pay a consumption charge and sometimes a capacity charge; check whether AC is included or billed separately.

items.q: What is DEWA?
items.a: **Dubai Electricity and Water Authority**: you register electricity and water in your name at move-in (with a refundable deposit). The housing fee is also collected through DEWA bills.

items.q: What is the housing fee in Dubai?
items.a: A municipality fee collected via DEWA bills: **tenants pay 5% of annual rent**; owner-occupiers pay a fee based on the property's rental value (per the municipality's formula).

items.q: What is the Rental Index?
items.a: DLD/RERA's tool showing **average rents by area and unit type**, used to calculate the maximum allowed rent increase on renewal.

items.q: What is Form A?
items.a: RERA agreement between a **seller and the listing broker**, authorising marketing of the property.

items.q: What is Form B?
items.a: RERA agreement between a **buyer and the buyer's broker**.

items.q: What is Form F?
items.a: The RERA **sale MOU** between buyer and seller in a resale, used at the trustee office for transfer.

items.q: What is Form I?
items.a: RERA **agreement between two brokerages** to share commission on a deal.

items.q: What is a registration trustee?
items.a: A DLD-licensed **trustee office** that processes property transfers and registrations on DLD's behalf (for a service fee).

items.q: What is a manager's cheque?
items.a: A bank-issued cheque guaranteed by the bank, commonly used for **property transfer payments** (to seller, DLD fees, developer).

items.q: What is a Power of Attorney (POA) in property?
items.a: A legal document letting someone **act for the owner/buyer** (sign, transfer, collect). For property it must be notarised; if signed abroad, legalised/attested for UAE use.

items.q: What is a developer's statement of account (SOA)?
items.a: A statement showing **what the buyer has paid and what is due**, used for resales, mortgages and visas.

items.q: What is an off-plan resale (assignment)?
items.a: Selling an off-plan unit **before completion**: the new buyer takes over the contract and remaining payments, with the developer's NOC and an Oqood transfer at DLD.

items.q: What is a 'flip'?
items.a: Buying off-plan and **reselling before handover** for a premium. Profit depends on price growth, fees and the developer's resale rules.

items.q: What is capital appreciation?
items.a: The **increase in a property's value** over time, e.g. from launch price to handover or resale.

items.q: What is gross rental yield?
items.a: **Annual rent ÷ purchase price × 100.** Example: AED 90,000 ÷ AED 1,200,000 = **7.5%** gross.

items.q: What is net rental yield?
items.a: **(Annual rent − service charges − maintenance − management − other costs) ÷ price × 100.** It's the realistic return; always lower than gross.

items.q: What is ROI?
items.a: **Return on investment**: total profit ÷ cash invested × 100. For off-plan, ROI on cash paid can be much higher than on the full price.

items.q: What is LTV?
items.a: **Loan-to-value**: the mortgage amount as a % of the property's value. UAE Central Bank sets maximum LTVs.

items.q: What is DBR?
items.a: **Debt burden ratio**: total monthly debt payments ÷ monthly income. UAE rules cap it at 50% for mortgages.

items.q: What is a pre-approval (mortgage)?
items.a: A bank's **conditional approval** of how much you can borrow, valid for a limited time, before choosing a property.

items.q: What is a valuation (bank valuation)?
items.a: An independent assessment of the property's **market value** for the bank; the loan is based on the lower of price and valuation.

items.q: What is a branded residence?
items.a: Homes designed/managed with a luxury brand (hotel, fashion, auto), often with hotel-style services and higher prices and service charges.

items.q: What is a holiday home?
items.a: A property rented **short-term** to tourists under a DET holiday home permit.

items.q: What is DET?
items.a: Dubai's **Department of Economy and Tourism**: licenses businesses and regulates holiday homes and consumer protection.
items.kw: det department of economy and tourism

items.q: What is the Golden Visa?
items.a: A **10-year renewable UAE residence visa**; one route is owning Dubai property worth **AED 2 million or more**.

items.q: What is Ijari vs Ejari?
items.a: Same thing, two spellings: **Ejari** is the official Dubai tenancy contract registration system.

items.q: What is 'ready' vs 'off-plan' vs 'secondary'?
items.a:
- **Off-plan:** under construction, bought from developer (primary) or resale
- **Ready:** completed
- **Secondary market:** any resale between owners
items.kw: ready off plan secondary primary meaning

items.q: What is primary market?
items.a: Sales **directly from the developer** (new units).

items.q: What is the secondary market?
items.a: **Resales between owners** (ready or off-plan assignments).

items.q: What is absorption (sales velocity)?
items.a: How fast units **sell** in a project or area, e.g. units sold per month or % sold since launch. High absorption suggests strong demand.

items.q: What is supply pipeline?
items.a: Units **planned or under construction** expected to complete in coming years. High supply in an area at handover can soften rents/prices.

items.q: What is a 'launch price'?
items.a: The developer's **first price** for a phase. Later phases or released units are often priced higher if demand is strong.

items.q: What is a 'phase' in a project?
items.a: A **group of units/buildings released together**. Big communities are sold and built in phases with different prices and completion dates.

items.q: What is a 'shell and core' unit?
items.a: A unit delivered **without interior fit-out** (common in commercial). The buyer finishes it.

items.q: What is 'fully fitted' vs 'furnished'?
items.a: **Fitted:** kitchen, wardrobes, bathrooms installed. **Furnished:** also includes furniture/appliances. Most Dubai residential off-plan is fitted, not furnished.

items.q: What is the difference between a broker and a developer sales agent?
items.a: A **broker** (licensed agency, BRN/ORN) can sell many developers' projects and resales; a **developer's in-house sales agent** sells only that developer's units.

items.q: What is DIFC Wills?
items.a: The **DIFC Courts Wills Service** lets non-Muslims register wills covering Dubai assets, so property passes according to their wishes rather than default rules. Get legal advice.

items.q: What is 'net of fees' in a price?
items.a: Price **excluding** DLD and other fees. Always tell clients the all-in cost (price + 4% DLD + admin).

items.q: What is DLD fee waiver?
items.a: A **developer promotion** paying part or all of the buyer's 4% DLD fee. Check it's written in the SPA/offer.

items.q: What is a 'cash buyer'?
items.a: A buyer paying **without a mortgage**. Cash buyers can complete faster and negotiate harder.

items.q: What is 'end-user'?
items.a: A buyer who will **live in the property**, as opposed to an investor.

items.q: What is 'yield on cost'?
items.a: Rent ÷ **total cost** (price + fees + furnishing), a stricter yield measure than rent ÷ price.

items.q: What is a 'distress sale'?
items.a: A sale **below market** because the seller needs cash fast or can't continue payments.

items.q: What is 'premium' in a resale?
items.a: The **amount above the original price** a resale buyer pays the seller.

items.q: How much is the Dubai Land Department fee on a property purchase?
items.a: **4% of the purchase price**, paid at registration (Oqood for off-plan, title deed transfer for ready). Plus small admin/knowledge fees. Confirm current fees on dubailand.gov.ae.
items.kw: dld fee how much 4% registration dld fee project off plan how much

items.q: Who pays the 4% DLD fee: buyer or seller?
items.a: In practice the **buyer** pays it on almost all Dubai sales, unless the developer or seller agrees to cover it (promotions or negotiation). Put any agreement in writing.
items.kw: who pays dld fee buyer seller

items.q: Is the DLD fee charged on off-plan resales?
items.a: Yes. The resale is a new registration, so the **new buyer pays 4%** (normally on the resale price) at the Oqood transfer.
items.kw: dld fee resale off plan assignment

items.q: What is the trustee office fee?
items.a: Registration trustee offices charge a **service fee for each transfer** (commonly a few thousand dirhams plus VAT, higher for higher-value property). Check the current fee with the trustee before the appointment.

items.q: What is the mortgage registration fee?
items.a: DLD charges **0.25% of the loan amount** plus a small admin fee to register a mortgage. Confirm on dubailand.gov.ae.

items.q: What other costs does a mortgage buyer pay?
items.a: Typically: **bank arrangement/processing fee** (often up to 1% of the loan), **valuation fee**, **mortgage registration 0.25%**, life and property insurance. Ask the bank for its fee schedule.

items.q: What is the agency commission on a resale?
items.a: Market practice is about **2% of the price + 5% VAT**, agreed in Form A/B. It's negotiable and not fixed by law.

items.q: Does a buyer pay commission on a new off-plan purchase?
items.a: Usually **no**: the developer pays the brokerage under its marketing agreement. Make sure the client knows this upfront.

items.q: What fees are due at handover?
items.a: Typically: **final instalment**, **service charges in advance** (often 6–12 months), **title deed issuance fee**, **DEWA deposit**, district cooling deposit (if any), and move-in/community fees. Ask the developer for the handover statement.

items.q: What is the DEWA deposit?
items.a: A **refundable security deposit** when you open an electricity/water account. The amount depends on the property type and size. Check DEWA's website for current amounts.

items.q: How much are service charges in Dubai?
items.a: They vary widely by building and community, from **under AED 10 to over AED 30 per sq ft per year**. Check the exact rate in the RERA Service Charge Index (Dubai REST app) for completed buildings or the developer's estimate for off-plan.
items.kw: service charges how much per sqft

items.q: Who sets service charges?
items.a: The **owners' association/management company** prepares the budget and **RERA approves** it. Rates are published in the Service Charge Index.

items.q: Are service charges paid on off-plan units before handover?
items.a: Generally **no**: they start from handover/completion. The developer often collects the first period in advance at handover.

items.q: What is the title deed issuance fee?
items.a: A **small DLD fee** to issue the title deed at completion (not another 4%). Check the current amount on DLD's website or the handover statement.

items.q: What does the developer charge for a resale NOC?
items.a: It varies by developer, often **from about AED 1,000 to several thousand dirhams**, sometimes a % of price. Check the SPA and the developer's resale policy.

items.q: What is the Oqood registration admin fee?
items.a: On top of the 4% DLD fee, there's a **small registration admin fee** (and some developers add their own processing fee). It appears on the developer's statement of account.

items.q: Is there VAT on property in Dubai?
items.a: **Residential:** first sale within 3 years of completion is zero-rated; later sales exempt, so buyers pay no VAT on the price. **Commercial:** 5% VAT. Services (commission, admin fees) carry 5% VAT.

items.q: What is the cost of a power of attorney?
items.a: Notary fees in the UAE are modest; abroad, add notarisation plus **attestation/legalisation** at the UAE embassy/MOFA. Ask a notary for the current fee.

items.q: What costs does a seller pay in an off-plan resale?
items.a: Usually: **developer NOC fee**, any **agency commission** they agreed, and settling any **overdue instalments**. The buyer pays the 4% DLD fee unless agreed otherwise.

items.q: How much cash does a buyer need on day one for off-plan?
items.a: Typically **down payment (10–20%) + 4% DLD fee + admin fees**. Example: AED 1,000,000 with 10% down = AED 100,000 + AED 40,000 + small fees ≈ **AED 140,000+**.
items.kw: cash needed day one off plan

items.q: What is the 'all-in cost' of a purchase?
items.a: **Price + 4% DLD + admin/registration + (mortgage costs) + (agency fee on resales) + furnishing (if renting)**. Show clients this total, not only the price.

items.q: Are there annual property taxes in Dubai?
items.a: **No annual property tax.** Owners pay service charges, the housing fee (via DEWA) and utilities.

items.q: What is the knowledge fee / innovation fee?
items.a: Small **DLD service fees** (tens of dirhams) added to many transactions. They're on the receipt.

items.q: Do I pay the DLD fee again when the unit completes?
items.a: **No.** It's paid once at Oqood. Converting to a title deed only has the issuance fee.

items.q: Can the 4% DLD fee be paid in instalments?
items.a: Sometimes: DLD and some developers have offered **instalment options** at certain times, and some developers include it in the plan. Check what's currently available with the developer/DLD.

items.q: What is a booking amount?
items.a: The **first payment to reserve a unit**, often 5–10% (or a fixed amount), credited to the down payment. It goes to the developer/escrow, never to a personal account.

items.q: What is the cost of an Ejari registration?
items.a: A **small fee** (typically a few hundred dirhams) through a typing centre, the Dubai REST app or the developer/management. Check current fees.

items.q: What insurance does an owner need?
items.a: Building insurance is usually covered by the service charge; **contents insurance** is the owner's/tenant's choice. Mortgaged owners must have **life insurance** and the bank's required property insurance.

items.q: What are community/master fees?
items.a: Some master communities charge **fees for shared infrastructure** (roads, parks) on top of the building's service charge. Ask the developer whether they apply.

items.q: What is a move-in permit fee?
items.a: Some buildings charge a **move-in/move-out fee or deposit** for using lifts and loading bays. It's set by building management.

items.q: How do I estimate yearly holding costs?
items.a: Add: **service charge (rate × sq ft)** + insurance + maintenance (often budget ~0.5–1% of value) + utilities if vacant + housing fee. Use it in net yield.

items.q: Is commission charged on the DLD fee amount?
items.a: No. Commission is a % of the **property price**, not of fees.

items.q: What fees apply when transferring property to a family member?
items.a: Gifts to **first-degree relatives** may get a reduced DLD fee in some cases; standard sales pay 4%. Check DLD's current gift rules before advising.

items.q: What is a cancellation fee in an off-plan purchase?
items.a: There's no single fee: if the buyer defaults, Law 13 of 2008 (Art. 11) allows the developer to keep **up to 25–40%** depending on construction progress. Voluntary cancellation terms are per developer.

items.q: What is a registration fee for a lease?
items.a: Ejari has a small fee; long leases (over a year, registered at DLD) may carry DLD fees. Check DLD for long-lease registration.

items.q: What are the steps to buy a resale (ready) property in Dubai?
items.a:
1. Agree price; sign **Form F (MOU)** with ~10% deposit (often a security cheque)
2. Seller gets the **developer NOC** (and bank clearance if mortgaged)
3. Buyer arranges mortgage if needed
4. **Transfer at a trustee office:** pay seller (manager's cheques), 4% DLD, trustee fee
5. New title deed issued to the buyer

items.q: How long does an off-plan purchase take to register?
items.a: After signing the SPA and paying the down payment and DLD fee, the developer usually registers **Oqood within days to a few weeks**. Ask the developer for the Oqood certificate.

items.q: What documents does a buyer need?
items.a: Usually: **passport**, **Emirates ID and visa** (if resident), proof of address (some developers), and source-of-funds information for AML checks. Companies need trade licence and corporate documents.

items.q: Why do developers ask for KYC and source of funds?
items.a: UAE **anti-money-laundering rules** require developers, brokers and banks to verify the buyer's identity and, for larger or cash payments, the source of funds.

items.q: Can a buyer pay in cash (banknotes)?
items.a: Large cash payments are restricted and must be reported under AML rules. Buyers should pay by **bank transfer, cheque or card** to the escrow account.

items.q: Can a buyer pay in a foreign currency or crypto?
items.a: Developers mostly accept **AED/USD bank transfers**. Some accept crypto through licensed payment providers that convert to AED. Check the developer's accepted payment methods.

items.q: What should be checked before signing an SPA?
items.a:
- **Unit, area and price** match the offer
- **Payment plan** and due dates
- **Completion date and grace period**
- **Late payment penalties**
- **Resale/assignment rules** and NOC fees
- **Area variance clause**
- Escrow account details

items.q: Who signs the SPA?
items.a: The **buyer(s)** and the **developer**. Remote buyers can sign electronically or via POA.

items.q: How long does a ready transfer take?
items.a: Cash deals can transfer in **1–2 weeks**; mortgage deals often take **3–6 weeks** (approvals, valuation, NOCs).

items.q: What happens at the trustee office on transfer day?
items.a: Buyer, seller (or POAs) and the bank rep (if mortgage) attend; manager's cheques are handed over, DLD fees paid, and DLD issues the **new title deed**.

items.q: Can two people buy jointly?
items.a: Yes. **Joint ownership** is registered with each owner's share (e.g. 50/50). Both sign documents.

items.q: Can a minor own property in Dubai?
items.a: A minor can be registered as owner, usually with a **guardian** managing the property. Specific DLD/court requirements apply; check before advising.

items.q: How does a buyer verify a developer is genuine?
items.a: Check on **DLD/Dubai REST** that the developer and project are registered, the **escrow account** exists, and look at the developer's delivered projects.

items.q: What is the role of the agent in an off-plan sale?
items.a: Advise the client, compare projects, explain plans and fees, handle the EOI/booking with the developer, check documents and follow through to Oqood and handover.

items.q: What is the deposit in a resale (Form F)?
items.a: Usually **10% of the price**, often as a security cheque held by the agency/trustee until transfer.

items.q: What if a resale buyer backs out after Form F?
items.a: The Form F terms apply: the **seller usually keeps the deposit** if the buyer defaults without valid reason; if the seller defaults, they may owe compensation. Read the clauses.
items.kw: buyer backs out form f deposit

items.q: Can a buyer purchase through a company?
items.a: Yes, depending on the developer and area; documents include trade licence, MoA, board resolution. Tax and visa effects differ from personal ownership.

items.q: What is an off-plan 'unit allocation'?
items.a: After EOIs, the developer **assigns specific units** to buyers in queue order; buyers confirm by booking.

items.q: How do I check if a unit is mortgaged before buying a resale?
items.a: Ask for the **title deed** and a **DLD ownership/title status** check (via Dubai REST/trustee). A mortgage must be cleared at transfer.

items.q: What is a 'blocked' or 'pending' transfer?
items.a: DLD may block a transfer if there are **unpaid developer dues, service charges, a mortgage or legal holds**. Clear them first.

items.q: Can a buyer view an off-plan unit?
items.a: Not the actual unit; buyers see the **show apartment, renders, floor plans and the site**. Some developers offer site visits for later stages.
items.kw: view off plan unit show apartment

items.q: What does 'subject to availability' mean?
items.a: Prices and units can **change or sell out** before booking; nothing is reserved until the booking is confirmed.

items.q: What should an agent send a client after the call?
items.a: A short summary: **unit options, price per sq ft vs area, payment plan with cash needed, fees, completion date, and the next step** with a date. DealPro's client report covers most of it.
items.kw: what to send client after call

items.q: How long does it take to get the Oqood certificate after paying?
items.a: Usually **within a few weeks** of the down payment and DLD fee, depending on the developer. If it's delayed, ask the developer for the registration status.

items.q: Can an off-plan buyer change the unit after booking?
items.a: Only if the **developer agrees** (unit swap/upgrade), sometimes with a fee. It's at the developer's discretion.

items.q: What does a 60/40 payment plan mean?
items.a: **60% paid during construction** (incl. down payment) and **40% on handover**. Example AED 1M: 600k over construction, 400k at keys (cash or mortgage).

items.q: What does an 80/20 payment plan mean?
items.a: **80% during construction, 20% at handover.** Lower final payment, but more cash needed during the build.

items.q: What does a 50/50 plan mean?
items.a: Usually **50% before handover, 50% at or after handover**. If part is after handover, it's a post-handover plan.

items.q: What does a 1% monthly plan mean?
items.a: The buyer pays **1% of the price every month** (after the down payment) for a set period, often continuing after handover. Check the total months and what's due at keys.

items.q: Which payment plan is better for an investor?
items.a: It depends on cash flow and exit: **back-loaded plans** (more at handover/post-handover) need less cash early and suit flips/renting; **front-loaded** plans often come with lower prices. Compare total price, timing and the exit plan.

items.q: What happens if a buyer pays more than the schedule early?
items.a: Some developers give **early payment discounts**; others just credit it. Ask the developer; get any discount in writing.

items.q: Can the 4% DLD fee be included in the mortgage?
items.a: Generally **no**: banks lend on the property value; fees are paid in cash.

items.q: What is the maximum mortgage for an expat in Dubai?
items.a: For a **first home**: up to **75%** of value up to AED 5M (**65%** above AED 5M). Second/investment homes: **60%**. Off-plan: max **50%**. (UAE Central Bank limits; banks may lend less.)

items.q: What is the maximum mortgage for a UAE national?
items.a: First home: up to **80%** up to AED 5M (**70%** above). Second home: **65%**. Off-plan: **50%**. Banks may apply stricter limits.

items.q: What is the maximum mortgage term in the UAE?
items.a: Up to **25 years**, and usually it must end by retirement age (often 65 for salaried, 70 for self-employed, per bank).

items.q: What's a 'handover mortgage'?
items.a: Taking a mortgage **at completion** to pay the handover balance. Normal ready-property LTV rules apply then.

items.q: What is a fixed vs variable mortgage rate?
items.a: **Fixed:** same rate for an initial period (1–5 years). **Variable:** linked to EIBOR plus a margin, moves with rates. Most fixed loans revert to variable later.

items.q: What is EIBOR?
items.a: The **Emirates Interbank Offered Rate**, the benchmark for UAE variable mortgage rates.

items.q: Can non-residents get a UAE mortgage?
items.a: Yes, from some banks, usually at **lower LTV** and with income/documentation requirements. Rates and terms vary; refer to a mortgage adviser.

items.q: What income documents do banks need for a mortgage?
items.a: Salaried: **salary certificate, payslips, 6 months' bank statements**. Self-employed: **trade licence, company and personal statements, audited accounts**. Plus ID and credit report.

items.q: What is the AECB credit score?
items.a: The UAE's **Al Etihad Credit Bureau** score used by banks to assess borrowers. Residents can check their report via AECB.

items.q: What is the early settlement fee on a UAE mortgage?
items.a: Capped by Central Bank rules (commonly **1% of the outstanding amount, max AED 10,000**). Check the bank's terms.

items.q: Can the developer refuse a resale if the buyer hasn't paid enough?
items.a: Yes. Many SPAs require a **minimum % paid** (often 30–40%) before a developer issues a resale NOC.

items.q: What is a 'handover payment' and how to prepare?
items.a: The large instalment due at completion (e.g. 20–60%). Prepare **cash or a mortgage pre-approval** months before the handover notice.

items.q: What is a 'payment plan reminder' from the developer?
items.a: Developers send **demand notices** before each instalment; pay to the escrow account by the due date to avoid penalties.

items.q: What is a late payment penalty?
items.a: The SPA may charge **interest or a fixed penalty** on late instalments. Persistent default triggers the Article 11 process.

items.q: What law protects off-plan buyers' money?
items.a: **Law No. 8 of 2007** (escrow accounts) and **Law No. 13 of 2008** (interim real estate register, amended by Law 19 of 2017).
items.kw: law protects off plan buyers escrow law

items.q: Can a developer sell an off-plan project without RERA approval?
items.a: No. Projects must be **registered and have an escrow account** before marketing and selling.

items.q: What can a buyer do if the developer delays handover?
items.a: Check the SPA's **completion date and grace period** and any compensation clause; raise it with the developer, then complain to **RERA/DLD**; disputes go to the Dubai courts. A lawyer should advise on claims.

items.q: Where are Dubai property disputes resolved?
items.a: Most go to the **Dubai Courts** (some via DLD's dispute services); rental disputes go to the **Rental Disputes Center**.

items.q: What is the Rental Disputes Center?
items.a: DLD's centre for **landlord–tenant disputes** (rents, evictions, deposits).

items.q: Can a landlord increase rent anytime?
items.a: No. Increases are allowed **only at renewal**, within the **RERA rental index** limits, and with **90 days' written notice** before the contract ends.

items.q: How much can rent increase at renewal?
items.a: Per the RERA index: **0%** if the rent is within 10% of average; **up to 5%** if 11–20% below; **10%** if 21–30% below; **15%** if 31–40% below; **20%** if more than 40% below. Use DLD's rental calculator.

items.q: Can a landlord evict a tenant to sell or move in?
items.a: Yes, with **12 months' notice** delivered via **notary public or registered mail**, at the end of the contract, for listed reasons (own use, sale, major renovation).

items.q: What are a developer's obligations after handover?
items.a: Fix **installation defects for 1 year** and **structural defects for 10 years** (Dubai Law 6 of 2019), plus SPA warranties.

items.q: Can foreigners inherit Dubai property?
items.a: Yes. Without a will, **Sharia-based rules** may apply by default for Muslims; non-Muslims can register wills (e.g. DIFC Wills) so assets pass per their wishes. Get legal advice.

items.q: Can a developer change the floor plan after the SPA?
items.a: Minor changes may be allowed under the SPA; **material changes** usually need the buyer's consent and RERA approval. Check the SPA's variation clause.

items.q: What is the 'Interim Real Property Register'?
items.a: The legal name for **Oqood**: the DLD register of off-plan sales under Law 13 of 2008.

items.q: Is an off-plan sale outside Oqood valid?
items.a: No. Off-plan sales (and resales) **not registered on the interim register are void** under Law 13 of 2008.

items.q: Can a buyer stop paying if construction stops?
items.a: Don't advise stopping payments: it can trigger Article 11. The buyer should check DLD progress and complain to RERA/DLD; take legal advice.

items.q: What is a 'stalled' or 'cancelled' project?
items.a: A project RERA has **frozen or cancelled**. Buyers' money in escrow is protected; the special committee handles settlements and refunds.

items.q: Can a buyer sue the agent for wrong information?
items.a: Agents are bound by RERA's **code of ethics**; misleading information can lead to RERA penalties and civil claims. Put key facts in writing and quote official sources.

items.q: What is the Dubai real estate code of ethics for brokers?
items.a: RERA's rules: **honesty, no misleading ads, written agreements (Forms A/B), confidentiality, licensed activity only**. Breaches carry fines or licence action.

items.q: Can a seller sell a property that's mortgaged?
items.a: Yes, the mortgage is **paid off at transfer** (from the buyer's funds or the seller's) with the bank's liability letter and release.

items.q: Who keeps the original title deed when there's a mortgage?
items.a: The deed shows the **mortgage registered in the bank's favour**; it's released at payoff.

items.q: What's the difference between DLD and RERA in disputes?
items.a: **DLD** registers property and runs services; **RERA** regulates the market (brokers, developers, escrow, OAs) and handles regulatory complaints. Court cases go to Dubai Courts.

items.q: When can an off-plan buyer sell?
items.a: When the **developer allows it**, usually after a minimum % paid (often 30–40%). Check the SPA.

items.q: How does the money flow in an off-plan resale?
items.a: The new buyer pays the **seller** what they paid to the developer **plus the premium**, pays **4% DLD**, and takes over the remaining instalments. The developer's NOC fee is usually paid by the seller.

items.q: What documents are needed for an off-plan resale?
items.a: **Oqood certificate**, SPA, developer **NOC**, **statement of account**, IDs/passports of both parties, Form F, and bank clearance if mortgaged.

items.q: How do I price an off-plan resale?
items.a: Compare with **the developer's current price** for similar units, **recent DLD resale transactions** in the project, and the area's price per sq ft. The resale must be attractive vs buying new from the developer.

items.q: What if the developer's new price is lower than the resale price?
items.a: Resale buyers will buy from the developer instead. The seller must **price below the developer's current price** or offer a better plan/position.

items.q: How long does an off-plan resale transfer take?
items.a: Often **1–3 weeks** once NOC and documents are ready.

items.q: Can a foreign buyer resell without coming to Dubai?
items.a: Yes, via **POA** or the developer's remote process.

items.q: What is the exit plan for an off-plan buyer?
items.a: Options: **flip before handover**, **sell at handover**, **rent and hold**, or **live in it**. Plan the exit before buying; DealPro's exit scenarios help.

items.q: Is there capital gains tax when selling?
items.a: **No capital gains tax for individuals** in the UAE. Check home-country tax.

items.q: When is the best time to sell an off-plan unit?
items.a: Often **near completion**, when the project is visible and the area matures, or when demand spikes. It depends on market, supply in the area and the payment plan.
items.kw: best time to sell off plan

items.q: What is a 'distressed off-plan resale'?
items.a: An owner who **can't keep paying** sells below market, sometimes at or below original price. Good for buyers; check outstanding dues.

items.q: Can an off-plan unit be gifted to a family member?
items.a: Yes, through DLD's **gift transfer** process; fees and rules depend on the relationship. Check DLD's current rules.

items.q: How do agents find buyers for off-plan resales?
items.a: List on **portals** with a Trakheesi permit, use your database, target investors who missed the launch, and show the price vs developer's current price with DLD data.

items.q: What should a seller check before listing an off-plan resale?
items.a: Minimum % paid, **NOC fee**, outstanding dues, developer's current pricing, and a realistic premium vs DLD resale data.

items.q: How do I calculate rental yield for a client?
items.a: **Gross yield = annual rent ÷ price × 100.** Net yield subtracts service charges, maintenance, management and vacancy. Use DLD/Ejari rents for similar units, not asking rents.

items.q: Where can I find real rents for an area?
items.a: **DLD rental index / Ejari data**, the Dubai REST app, and DealPro's **Price map** (rents and yields by community). Portal listings show asking rents, which are higher.

items.q: What is a typical gross yield in Dubai?
items.a: It varies by area and unit type, often **around 5–8% gross** for apartments, lower for villas. Check the specific community's data.

items.q: Are studios or bigger units better for yield?
items.a: Smaller units (studios, 1-beds) usually have **higher gross yields**; villas have lower yields but often stronger capital growth. Match it to the client's goal.

items.q: How much does property management cost?
items.a: Long-term management is often **around 5% of annual rent** (varies). Holiday-home operators often take **15–25%** of revenue plus costs. Get quotes.

items.q: What is a security deposit for a rental?
items.a: Commonly **5% of annual rent (unfurnished)** or **10% (furnished)**, held by the landlord and refunded minus damages.

items.q: How are rents paid in Dubai?
items.a: Usually by **post-dated cheques** (1–12 cheques per year) or bank transfer; fewer cheques can get a better rent.

items.q: Does the landlord pay DEWA?
items.a: Usually the **tenant** registers DEWA in their name for long-term rentals; for holiday homes the owner/operator pays.

items.q: Who pays service charges, landlord or tenant?
items.a: The **owner (landlord)** pays service charges; tenants don't, unless a holiday-home model bundles costs.

items.q: Who pays maintenance in a rented apartment?
items.a: By default the **landlord** handles major maintenance; minor upkeep may be on the tenant per the contract. Write it in the tenancy contract.

items.q: Can I rent out a unit on a post-handover payment plan?
items.a: Usually yes after handover; some developers require consent while the unit is pledged. Check the SPA.

items.q: How long are Dubai tenancy contracts?
items.a: Typically **12 months**, renewable. Shorter terms are possible but less common for unfurnished units.

items.q: What is short-term rental income vs long-term?
items.a: **Short-term (holiday home):** higher gross income, higher costs and vacancy, needs a DET permit. **Long-term:** stable, lower effort. Compare net income.
items.kw: short term vs long term rental

items.q: Does a holiday home need a permit?
items.a: Yes, a **DET holiday home permit** for each unit, renewed yearly, and the building must allow it.

items.q: What is the Tourism Dirham?
items.a: A per-night fee charged to guests in hotels and holiday homes, collected by the operator and paid to DET.

items.q: How do I estimate the first rent at handover?
items.a: Look at **current Ejari rents for similar units nearby**, then adjust for new-build premium and the area's supply at handover (DealPro: Upcoming supply).

items.q: What happens to rents when lots of supply hands over?
items.a: More competing units usually means **slower rent growth or discounts** in that area for a while. Check the supply pipeline for the handover year.

items.q: Can a tenant sublet?
items.a: Only with the **landlord's written consent**; unauthorised subletting can be grounds for eviction.

items.q: How does a landlord register Ejari?
items.a: Through the **Dubai REST app**, a typing centre or the management company, with the title deed, tenancy contract, IDs and DEWA details.

items.q: What's a good occupancy rate assumption?
items.a: For long-term rentals, budget **1 month vacancy per year** conservatively; for holiday homes it varies seasonally (use operator data).

items.q: What visa can a property buyer get?
items.a:
- **10-year Golden Visa:** property **AED 2M+**
- **2-year property investor visa:** completed property (rules changed in 2026; check DLD)
- **5-year retirement visa:** age 55+ with qualifying property

Confirm current rules with DLD/GDRFA.

items.q: Does an off-plan property qualify for the Golden Visa?
items.a: Yes, off-plan from **approved developers** counts at full contract value if it's AED 2M+, with Oqood and the developer's documents. Check current DLD/ICP requirements.

items.q: Can a mortgaged property qualify for the Golden Visa?
items.a: Yes, with a **bank NOC** showing the amount paid and balance, if the property value is AED 2M+.

items.q: Can I combine properties to reach AED 2M?
items.a: Yes, **several properties** in your name can be combined to reach AED 2M.

items.q: Who can a Golden Visa holder sponsor?
items.a: **Spouse, children and parents** (per the current rules).

items.q: How much does the property Golden Visa cost?
items.a: DLD lists about **AED 9,884.75** for the main applicant (medical, Emirates ID, residency, DLD and admin fees), plus fees per family member. Check DLD's page.

items.q: How long does the Golden Visa take?
items.a: DLD states about **7–10 business days** once documents are complete; the applicant must be in the UAE.

items.q: Does the Golden Visa need you to live in the UAE?
items.a: Golden Visa holders aren't bound by the usual 6-month-outside rule. Confirm specifics with ICP/GDRFA.
items.kw: golden visa live in uae 6 months

items.q: What happens to the visa if the property is sold?
items.a: The visa is linked to the investment; **selling below the threshold** can affect renewal or validity. Check with GDRFA before selling.

items.q: Where can buyers apply for the property Golden Visa?
items.a: Through **DLD's Golden Visa (Investor) service** at DLD service centres, with GDRFA/ICP issuing the residence.

items.q: Does buying property give citizenship?
items.a: **No.** UAE property gives residence visas, not citizenship.

items.q: Do individuals pay tax on rental income in Dubai?
items.a: **No.** Individuals' real estate investment income isn't subject to UAE Corporate Tax (Cabinet Decision 49 of 2023), unless it's a licensed business. Check home-country tax.

items.q: Do companies pay tax on property income?
items.a: Yes: companies are subject to **UAE Corporate Tax at 9%** on taxable profits above AED 375,000 (with exceptions). Get a tax adviser.

items.q: Is there inheritance tax in Dubai?
items.a: **No inheritance tax** in the UAE. Succession rules still apply; wills are recommended.

items.q: Is there stamp duty in Dubai?
items.a: No stamp duty as such; the **4% DLD registration fee** is the transfer charge.

items.q: Do buyers pay VAT on residential off-plan?
items.a: No VAT on the price for residential (first sale zero-rated); commercial property carries 5%.

items.q: Do agents charge VAT on commission?
items.a: Yes, **5% VAT** applies to brokerage commission if the agency is VAT-registered (most are).

items.q: Should foreign buyers check home-country tax?
items.a: Yes. Their country may tax **rental income or gains abroad**. Suggest a tax adviser at home.

items.q: What licence does a Dubai real estate agent need?
items.a: A **RERA broker card (BRN)** after the Dubai Real Estate Institute (DREI) course and exam, working under a **licensed brokerage (ORN)**.

items.q: What is DREI?
items.a: The **Dubai Real Estate Institute**, DLD's training arm that runs the broker certification course and exam.

items.q: Do off-plan ads need a permit?
items.a: Yes, a **Trakheesi permit**, and off-plan ads must show the **escrow account number, developer and completion date** and must be for registered projects.

items.q: Can an agent advertise on Instagram without a permit?
items.a: Property ads on social media also need **Trakheesi permits**; influencers/advertisers may also need a **UAE media/advertiser permit**. Check RERA and NMA rules.

items.q: Can an agent take a deposit in their own account?
items.a: **No.** Deposits go to the **developer/escrow** or are held per RERA rules (e.g. security cheques with the agency). Never personal accounts.

items.q: What must an agent disclose to clients?
items.a: Their **BRN/agency**, commission terms (in writing), any conflicts of interest, and accurate project information.

items.q: How should agents handle client data?
items.a: Collect only what's needed, keep it secure, and **don't share without consent**. UAE data-protection rules and RERA ethics apply.

items.q: What AML duties do agents have?
items.a: Brokers must do **KYC**, watch for **suspicious transactions** (large cash, unclear source of funds) and report via the UAE FIU's goAML system as required.

items.q: Can an agent work for two brokerages?
items.a: No. A broker card is tied to **one licensed brokerage**.

items.q: How do agents split commission with another agency?
items.a: Sign **RERA Form I** before the deal, stating the split.

items.q: What happens if an agent breaks RERA rules?
items.a: **Fines, suspension or licence cancellation**, depending on the violation.

items.q: Do agents need a Form A for off-plan primary sales?
items.a: No: primary off-plan sales run under the **developer's marketing agreement** with the brokerage. Form A/B are for resales/listings.

items.q: How does an agent get registered with a developer?
items.a: The **brokerage registers** with the developer's broker portal (trade licence, ORN, BRNs, bank details) and signs its agency agreement.

items.q: When is the developer's commission paid to the agency?
items.a: Per the developer's terms, often after the buyer pays a set % (e.g. 10–20%) and the SPA/Oqood is done. Check each developer's policy.

items.q: Can an agent offer cashback to a buyer?
items.a: Rebates/cashbacks are a **grey area**: they must be transparent, agreed in writing and not breach the developer's agreement or RERA rules. Check with your brokerage.

items.q: What should an agent never promise?
items.a: **Guaranteed returns, guaranteed resale profit, visas without checking rules, or handover dates beyond the SPA.**

items.q: How do agents verify a listing is genuine?
items.a: Check the **title deed** (or Oqood), seller's ID, and that Form A is signed; for off-plan, check the project on DLD.

items.q: What records should an agent keep?
items.a: Signed forms, client KYC, correspondence about offers, receipts, and Trakheesi permits for ads.

items.q: How do I open a first call with a new lead?
items.a: Three parts in 30 seconds: **who you are** in one line, **why you're calling** with one fact about the area/project, and **one question** that makes them talk. Then offer two times for a video call.

items.q: What are the first three questions to ask a buyer?
items.a:
1. **Live in or investment?**
2. **Budget including fees, cash or mortgage?**
3. **When will you decide, and what's making you look now?**

items.q: How do I handle 'Just send me the brochure'?
items.a: Agree, then add value: **'Sure, and I'll also send the DLD sales data for the area so you can see if the price makes sense.'** Book a 10-minute call to walk through it.

items.q: How do I handle 'Let me think about it'?
items.a: Ask **which part**: area, price or timing? Remind them of **their own motive** ('why now'), then agree a small next step with a time.

items.q: How do I handle 'Prices are too high'?
items.a: Don't argue. Show **price per sq ft vs the area average** and what **waiting costs** (rent paid, payment plan lost, next phase pricier). Offer a cheaper option or the conservative exit scenario.

items.q: How do I handle 'I'll wait for a market correction'?
items.a: Agree corrections can happen; show **their numbers**: cash needed now, the payment plan, and a **conservative scenario** where it still works. If it doesn't work conservatively, it's not the right project.

items.q: How do I handle 'I don't trust this developer'?
items.a: Say **'Let's check it together'**: DLD registration, escrow, construction %, delivered projects and delays. If doubts remain, suggest another developer.

items.q: How do I handle 'Another agent offered a discount'?
items.a: Ask **which unit, floor and view**; most 'discounts' compare different units. Offer to compare like for like and compete on data and after-sale service.

items.q: How do I handle 'My family needs to agree'?
items.a: Ask **who else decides and what they care about**, send a short video and report, and book a call with them.

items.q: How do I handle 'I prefer ready property'?
items.a: Compare on their goal: **off-plan** = lower entry, payment plan, launch price; **ready** = rent now, see what you buy. Show the cash flow of both.

items.q: How do I handle 'The service charge is too high'?
items.a: Show the **net yield after service charges** and compare with similar buildings via the Service Charge Index. High charges can mean better amenities and upkeep.

items.q: How do I handle 'I want a better payment plan'?
items.a: Check **other phases/projects** with back-loaded or post-handover plans, but show the price trade-off: better plans often mean higher prices.

items.q: How do I handle 'The location is too far'?
items.a: Show **infrastructure plans** (roads, metro, airport), drive times, and price per sq ft vs closer areas. Some buyers prefer value + growth over centrality.

items.q: How do I handle 'Rents will drop with new supply'?
items.a: Show **supply numbers for the handover year** (DealPro Upcoming supply) and where this project sits on price. Good projects in good spots rent first.

items.q: What are buying signals?
items.a: Questions about **process, a specific unit, money/payment dates, bringing family, or the exit**. When you hear two, stop presenting and close.

items.q: How do I close an off-plan deal?
items.a: Confirm the **unit, price incl. fees**, explain EOI/booking → SPA → Oqood, then ask with **two options** ('today or tomorrow morning?') and send the link while on the call.

items.q: What should I do after a client books?
items.a: Send a **summary of the SPA**, the **payment schedule** and the next construction update date, then update them regularly until handover.

items.q: How often should I follow up a warm lead?
items.a: A simple rhythm: **Day 1, 3, 7, 30**, each with **new value** (a fact, a launch, a price move), never 'are you still interested?'.

items.q: How do I revive a dead lead?
items.a: Send **a new reason**: a new launch, a price/plan change or new data, with one question and a time. No reply? Try again in 30 days.

items.q: How do I ask for referrals?
items.a: At **handover or after a portfolio check**, remind them how they found you and ask for **one person** who's even thinking about Dubai.

items.q: How do I present a project in the right order?
items.a: **Area → supply → developer → project → price → plan → exit.** Location first; price and exit last.

items.q: How do I talk about ROI without overpromising?
items.a: Show **real rents and net yield**, and **three scenarios** (conservative first). Never say 'guaranteed'.

items.q: How do I qualify an overseas investor?
items.a: Check **time zone, budget source, visa motive, how they'll pay (transfer/currency), and whether they can travel or need POA**.

items.q: How do I handle 'Can you give me a discount?'
items.a: Primary prices are set by the developer; you can ask about **promotions, DLD waivers or better plans**. On resales, negotiate with data.

items.q: How do I handle a client comparing five agents?
items.a: Be the one who brings **data they don't have**, answers in writing, and follows up on time. Don't compete on gossip or discounts.

items.q: What makes clients trust an agent?
items.a: **Honesty about risks, data from official sources, fast follow-through, and showing when NOT to buy.**

items.q: How do I explain a payment plan simply?
items.a: Show **today's cash (down payment + 4%)**, **what's paid during construction**, and **what's due at keys**, with dates and amounts on one page.

items.q: How do I handle 'I'll buy when it's finished'?
items.a: Explain the trade-off: ready later usually costs more than launch price, and the plan's cash-flow benefit is lost. Show the price gap between launch and ready units nearby.

items.q: How do I use WhatsApp professionally?
items.a: Short messages, **one point each**, voice notes only when invited, documents as PDF, and always a **next step with a time**.

items.q: Where does official Dubai property data come from?
items.a: **DLD transaction data** (via Dubai Data / DLD open data), DLD's rental index, and project data on Mashrooi. Portals show asking prices, not transactions.

items.q: How do I read a DLD transaction?
items.a: Key fields: **date, area, project, property type, size, price, registration type (off-plan/ready), procedure (sale/mortgage/gift)**. Use sales for price analysis.

items.q: What's the difference between asking price and transaction price?
items.a: **Asking** = portal listings (what sellers want). **Transaction** = registered DLD sale (what was paid). Use transactions for valuations.

items.q: How do I compare two areas for a client?
items.a: Compare **price per sq ft, 12-month change, yields, supply pipeline, off-plan share, and infrastructure**. DealPro's Price map and Market statistics show these.

items.q: What does a high off-plan share in an area mean?
items.a: Most sales are **new launches**: strong developer activity, possibly more future supply. Watch handover-year supply.

items.q: What's a good sign in an area's data?
items.a: **Rising transaction volumes and prices with healthy rents**, and supply that isn't overwhelming at handover.

items.q: How do I calculate price change over a year?
items.a: **(This year's average psf − last year's) ÷ last year's × 100.** Use the same unit type and similar projects.

items.q: What is a median price and why use it?
items.a: The **middle value** of sales; less distorted by a few very expensive sales than the average.

items.q: How many transactions are enough to trust an average?
items.a: More is better: a handful of sales can mislead. Look for **dozens of comparable transactions** and the same unit type.

items.q: Why do off-plan prices per sq ft often look higher than ready?
items.a: New projects have **newer specs, payment plans and launch premiums**; ready stock may be older. Compare like with like.

items.q: How do I explain supply to a client?
items.a: **Units handing over in the area per year**, compared with past years and demand. Too many at once can slow rents briefly.

items.q: What is a price-to-rent ratio?
items.a: **Price ÷ annual rent.** Lower ratios mean higher yields. Example: 1,200,000 ÷ 80,000 = 15.

items.q: Where can I check a developer's track record?
items.a: Look at **completed projects on DLD**, their completion dates vs promised, current projects' progress on Mashrooi, and news.

items.q: What is construction completion % on Mashrooi?
items.a: The **percentage inspected/reported** for the project; compare it with the time left to the completion date.

items.q: How do I estimate value at handover?
items.a: Use **current ready prices for similar units nearby** as a base, then conservative/realistic/optimistic growth. DealPro's exit scenarios do this.

items.q: What should a buyer do 3 months before handover?
items.a: Arrange **handover funds or mortgage**, plan the snagging inspection, decide **rent/live**, and check expected fees.

items.q: What is a handover notice?
items.a: The developer's **written notice** that the unit is ready, with the final statement and the steps/timeline to take possession.

items.q: Should a buyer hire a snagging company?
items.a: Often worth it: a professional inspection finds **defects buyers miss**, and the list is sent to the developer to fix.

items.q: What if snags aren't fixed?
items.a: Escalate in writing to the developer; defects fall under the **1-year installations / 10-year structural** liability. Keep photos and dates.

items.q: What utilities must be set up at handover?
items.a: **DEWA** (electricity/water), **district cooling** (if any), gas (some buildings), internet, and the building's **move-in permit**.

items.q: When is the title deed issued?
items.a: After **completion, full payment** (or mortgage registration) and the developer's application to DLD.

items.q: Can I rent out immediately after handover?
items.a: Yes, once you have the keys and the unit is ready; register the lease on **Ejari**.

items.q: What if the handover is late by months?
items.a: Check the SPA's **grace period** and compensation clause; raise it in writing; complain to RERA if needed.

items.q: Can a buyer refuse handover?
items.a: Only for **valid reasons** (e.g. unit materially different or not fit for use). Minor snags are fixed after handover. Get legal advice before refusing.

items.q: What documents does the buyer get at handover?
items.a: **Keys/access cards, handover certificate, title deed (or application), warranties/manuals, and the snag list.**

items.a: Under Article 11 of Law 13 of 2008 (as amended), at 85% completion the developer may terminate and keep **up to 40% of the sale value = up to AED 400,000** after DLD's notice process, or keep the contract and claim the balance / ask DLD to auction the unit (above 80%).
